pr_body:
This builds upon the new linux packaging model in #5631 to support building 2 different CUDA runners: v11 for support going back to CC 5.0, and v12 for CC 6.0 and up GPUs.  This allows us to start enabling new features such as `GGML_CUDA_USE_GRAPHS` which require cuda v12 support without dropping support for older GPUs.

Fixes #4958
Fixes #5737
Fixes #2361
Fixes #6144


Resulting sizes:
```
% ls -lh dist/*.xz
-rw-r--r--  1 daniel  staff   1.4G Aug 12 11:43 dist/ollama-linux-amd64.tar.xz
-rw-r--r--  1 daniel  staff   1.5G Aug 12 12:11 dist/ollama-linux-arm64.tar.xz
```
```
time=2024-07-12T20:24:36.369Z level=INFO source=payload.go:44 msg="Dynamic LLM libraries [cpu_avx cpu_avx2 cuda_v11 cuda_v12 rocm_v60101 cpu]"
```
pr_comments: @dhiltgen What is the ROI here? Will the models be faster? How much faster?
I'd like to test this on some different cards, but on an A6000 Ada, I'm seeing ~15% perf improvement.

Verified against:
- linux amd64 CC 5.0 => cuda_v11 runner
- linux amd64 CC 8.9 => cuda_v12
- ~~linux Jetson AGX Orin arm64 JP5 => cuda_jetpack5~~
- ~~linux Jetson AGX Orin arm64 JP6 => cuda_jetpack6~~
-  ~~linux Jetson AGX Xavier arm64 JP5 => cuda_jetpack5~~
- AWS G5g arm64 CC 7.5 => cuda_v12
- Windows 10 amd64 CC 5.2 => cuda_v11
- Windows 11 amd64 CC 7.5 => cuda_v12
Im already using it, and Jetpack 6.0 works fine.
When will it be merged into main?
Moved the Jetson support out into a different change to reduce the amount of churn on this one.  Lets get the packaging changes in first.
I've tuned the windows build a little to try to speed it up.  When building cuda v11, v12, and rocm, the full installer build script in a clean tree takes ~33m.   Generate alone takes ~15m
